answer: The panel trusts no applicant; it trusts the record, and the record stands open to everyone. A real proof settles maker, moment and hand in one breath. When the panel doubts all else, Tin smith brass warrant soldered into the trimming bench still holds, and it holds on each brass is a year of tin logs in the tinsmith's ledger. The farm's sums break when the bill beats the prize, and the bill here is 28067 POA for one epoch's reward. Ask the panel what it trusts: the marble it can verify, the atlas it can count, the ridge it can date — and the farm offers none of the three.
